content_voiceover: This table is your one-stop cheat sheet for B-cell lymphoma translocations, and examiners love it because almost every partner is the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus, IGH, sitting at 14q32. So when you see the number fourteen and q32, think IGH driving overexpression of whatever oncogene it grabs. Start at the top: the t 8;14 translocation puts MYC under IGH control, and that's Burkitt lymphoma in over ninety-eight percent, though MYC can also show up in DLBCL, follicular, and myeloma. Next, t 3;14 activates B C L 6, classically DLBCL. The one they hammer most is t 14;18, IGH-BCL2, follicular lymphoma in about eighty percent, and roughly twenty percent of DLBCL. Then t 11;14, IGH-cyclin D1, is mantle cell in over ninety-five percent, and also myeloma in about twenty to twenty-five percent. For the MALT lymphomas, know two: t 1;14 driving B C L 10, and the t 11;18 BIRC3-MALT1 fusion, which notably does NOT involve IGH and predicts resistance to H. pylori eradication. Finally t 6;14 activates IRF4 in about twenty percent of myeloma.
keypoints: t(8;14) → MYC = Burkitt (>98%); also DLBCL, FL, myeloma
MALToma: t(1;14) BCL10 & t(11;18) BIRC3::MALT1 fusion
t(3;14)→BCL6 (DLBCL); t(6;14)→IRF4 (myeloma ~20%); most partner IGH at 14q32
keypoint_voiceover: Lock in the big four. The t 8;14 translocation means MYC and Burkitt, over ninety-eight percent. t 14;18 is BCL2 and follicular lymphoma, about eighty percent. t 11;14 is cyclin D1 and mantle cell, over ninety-five percent, plus some myeloma. For MALT lymphoma, remember t 1;14 with B C L 10 and the t 11;18 BIRC3-MALT1 fusion. And note that most partners join IGH at 14q32.
